newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul opens door to overseas mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Seoul opens door to overseas mutual funds.

text.p: South Korea will allow foreign investment companies to sell offshore mutual funds and beneficiary certificates to domestic buyers from December, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
Mutual funds must be set up under laws for member nations of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) through public subscription, the statement said.
South Korea was invited to join the Paris-based club of rich nations earlier this month.
Sales must be made through existing domestic investment companies and brokerages and branches of foreign brokerages, the statement said.
The government will also let foreigners buy beneficiary certificates on up to 20 percent of the value of mutual funds issued by domestic investment firms.
That move is expected to help stabilise the local stock market, the statement added.
